newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jospin announces his own appointment as premier.
newsitem.headline: Jospin announces his own appointment as premier.

text.p: French Socialist party leader Lionel Jospin said on Monday that President Jacques Chirac had asked him to form a government after the left swept to power in a parliamentary election on Sunday.
"The president of the republic offered to appoint me as prime minister. I accepted," Jospin told reporters on the steps of the presidential palace after a 55-minute meeting with Chirac.
Jospin said he planned to form a government "quickly, this week".
The Socialist leader was summoned to meet the conservative president two hours after defeated centre-right Prime Minister Alain Juppe had tendered his resignation.
Final results issued on Monday showed the combined left won 318 seats in the 577-member National Assembly in Sunday's decisive runoff, with the 38 Communist members holding the balance of power.
Under the French system of "cohabitation" power-sharing, the president has a say in foreign affairs and defence but the government is in charge of domestic and economic policy.
